hook: A short file about a small spring whose water is remarkably good for you. Read the procedures closely, because the interesting part is not the water but how hard the Foundation works to hide its effects from its own people.
whyItMatters: Where many well-known entries are about threats, this one builds tension from what a beneficial anomaly might do to the world if word got out. It carries a rewrite tag, so the version you read may not match what longtime readers remember. Its spy-fiction flavor, with fake briefings and cover stories, sets it apart among early entries.
thingsToNotice:
The procedures are a layered lie: staff receive one of two false briefings, the true one is reserved for the top, and an evacuation code means something other than what workers believe. Testing suits for leaks by dunking the wearer in a pool is a neat practical detail that also shows how badly contact must be avoided.

The order that exposed staff be studied and then eliminated, by fire no less, hints at how hard the water's effects are to undo. A chemical plant built as cover fits the thriller tone. The banner at the top, invoking the founder, frames the whole file as a secret even within the Foundation.

related.note: Another cure-all the Foundation keeps under tight control.
Another healing object whose benefits come with strings attached.
